chapter: Studio recordings of the late twenties and thirties
title: Acoustic recording with the horn
summary: Morehouse describes recording before microphones: playing softly, tiny music, hanging music stands, and other musicians moving to the horn.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Yeah, okay. In those days, at least up to about 1925 when you made a recording, it was the old acoustic recording with the big horn, in the wall.
How did that work? What did the studio look like? How did you play? Before they had microphones.
Didn't you have to play a certain way because of the horn?
What did you have to do that was any different from later on.
Let me take a look at that.
No, when you were playing with the acoustic recordings before they had the electric microphones. And they had big horns in the wall.
Could you use for example, were you able to use a bass drum? Would it affect the horn?
It wouldn't have any effect on the horn or you wouldn't have...?
You would play soft, okay. And what about your music?
The music was just about that big.
Yeah, okay. Didn't you have to go up to the horn? Some of these instrumentalists, didn't they have to
go up to the horn and play into the horn?
How did it get past the music stands? Wasn't the music stands in their way? Did they have to go back and forth or what?
You don't remember, okay. I was just thinking, instead of the usual music stands, Chauncey, didn't they have the music stands hanging?
Hanging from the wall or from the ceiling?
So you could duck without falling over the music stand.
Is that the way it was, okay. And where was your drum? Were you near the back of the group or would you be near the side or the front? Where would you be?
My drums were...I forget now where they are.
You wouldn't have to move your drum. You could just stay still obviously. You didn't have to run back and forth.
But the other people, they had to run back and forth.
To go and play into the horn.
